boundary: the engine, reached through SQL against a running server
title: Engine and contrib defects in PostgreSQL 17.5, reached by SQL rather than by a C reduction
note: Sibling of mmgr-repros, not an extension of it. Those 8 cases are upstream use-after-free and double-free defects in the memory managers, pinned at 17.0 and reduced to C programs against aset/slab. These 19 are reached through SQL against a running 17.5 server and are mostly not allocator defects at all: 5 invariant, 4 integer, 3 spatial, 2 spatial/oob-read, 2 type-confusion, 1 null-deref, 1 wrong-answer, 1 authz. That spread is the point -- a corpus filtered to what a sanitizer can see would keep 6 of 19. Cases 12, 14 and 18 need a postmaster and cannot run under the single-user backend the arms use; their arms say so rather than reporting silence. Case 13's directive was written from its own run output and is a recording, not an independent oracle; its case.json says so. Our own constructed memory-context demonstrators are deliberately NOT here: they are this project's fixtures, which README.md places under ports/*/security-tests rather than in bug material.
